questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which structure forms the protein coat that encloses a virus's genetic material?
questions.option_a: Capsid
questions.option_c: Ribosome
questions.correct_answer: A
questions.explanation: The capsid is the protein shell surrounding the viral genome. An envelope, when present, is an additional outer lipid layer; ribosomes and cell walls are not components of all viruses.

distractor_rationales.B: An envelope is an optional outer membrane, not the protein coat around the genome.
distractor_rationales.C: Viruses do not contain ribosomes for independent protein synthesis.
distractor_rationales.D: A cell wall is not a standard viral structure.

questions.difficulty: easy
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: A virus uses an enzyme to make a DNA copy from its RNA genome after entering a host cell. Which enzyme carries out this step?
questions.option_a: DNA ligase
questions.option_c: Restriction endonuclease
questions.correct_answer: D
questions.explanation: Reverse transcriptase synthesizes DNA using an RNA template, a defining feature of retroviral replication. DNA ligase joins DNA fragments; RNA polymerase makes RNA; restriction enzymes cut DNA.

distractor_rationales.A: DNA ligase joins DNA fragments rather than copying RNA into DNA.
distractor_rationales.B: RNA polymerase synthesizes RNA from a DNA or RNA template, depending on the enzyme.
distractor_rationales.C: Restriction endonucleases cut DNA at particular sequences.

questions.difficulty: moderate
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which everyday situation does NOT transmit HIV?
questions.option_a: Sharing a meal and eating utensils
questions.option_c: Sharing injection equipment contaminated with infected blood
questions.option_d: Transmission from an infected parent to a child during pregnancy, birth or breastfeeding
questions.correct_answer: A
questions.explanation: HIV is not transmitted through ordinary social contact, shared meals or utensils. Transmission requires specific exposure routes such as infected blood or certain body fluids.

distractor_rationales.C: Shared equipment contaminated with infected blood can transmit HIV.
distractor_rationales.D: Transmission can occur during pregnancy, birth or breastfeeding.

questions.difficulty: moderate

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the main effect of an enzyme on a chemical reaction?
questions.option_a: It changes the final equilibrium position
questions.option_c: It increases the amount of product permanently
questions.correct_answer: It lowers the activation energy needed for the reaction
questions.distractor_rationales: Enzymes speed reactions by lowering activation energy and are not consumed overall. They do not change the reaction's equilibrium position or the net energy change.
questions.difficulty: It is used up as a reactant
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why can an enzyme act on some substrates but not on many others?
questions.option_a: Its active site has chemical and shape features suited to particular substrates
questions.option_c: Every enzyme can bind every biological molecule
questions.correct_answer: The substrate permanently becomes part of the enzyme
questions.distractor_rationales: Substrate recognition depends on complementary properties of the active site, including shape and chemical interactions. Binding is temporary and does not require the enzyme's sequence to change.
questions.difficulty: The enzyme changes its amino-acid sequence for each reaction
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: A competitive inhibitor occupies an enzyme's active site. Which change can reduce its effect in a simple competitive-inhibition model?
questions.option_a: Reducing substrate concentration
questions.option_c: Increasing substrate concentration
questions.correct_answer: Removing all enzyme molecules
questions.distractor_rationales: More substrate can outcompete a reversible competitive inhibitor for active-site binding. This does not mean every inhibitor can be overcome this way; the model applies to competitive inhibition.
questions.difficulty: Lowering the temperature to absolute zero
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: An enzyme works best near neutral pH. At a very acidic pH, its activity falls sharply. What is the best explanation?
questions.option_a: The substrate becomes an enzyme
questions.option_c: The enzyme gains extra active sites
questions.correct_answer: The reaction no longer needs activation energy
questions.distractor_rationales: Extreme pH can change ionization of amino-acid side chains and disrupt interactions that maintain the enzyme's structure, reducing substrate binding and catalysis.
questions.difficulty: Changes in ionization can alter bonds and the active-site shape
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: A population contains heritable variation in beak shape. During a period when hard seeds are common, birds with deeper beaks leave more offspring. Over generations, deeper beaks become more common. Which process best explains this change?
questions.option_a: Individuals deliberately change their genes when needed
questions.option_c: All members acquire identical mutations at the same time
questions.correct_answer: Natural selection changes the frequency of inherited traits across generations
questions.distractor_rationales: Individuals with a heritable feature that improves reproductive success contribute more offspring, so the feature can become more common over generations.
questions.difficulty: Traits acquired during an individual's lifetime are automatically inherited
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which statement best represents Lamarck's historical explanation of evolutionary change?
questions.option_a: Natural selection acts on inherited variation
questions.option_c: Traits strengthened or diminished through use or disuse were proposed to be passed to offspring
questions.correct_answer: Evolution occurs only when an organism chooses to change
questions.distractor_rationales: Lamarck proposed that use and disuse could alter traits and that acquired changes could be inherited. This is a historical theory, distinct from modern evolutionary genetics.
questions.difficulty: All species remain unchanged over time
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: After an antibiotic is used in a bacterial population, resistant bacteria make up a larger fraction of the survivors. Which explanation is most consistent with natural selection?
questions.option_a: Some bacteria already had heritable resistance; those variants survived and reproduced more
questions.option_c: Every bacterium intentionally developed resistance because it needed it
questions.correct_answer: The antibiotic taught bacteria a new genetic code
questions.distractor_rationales: Heritable variants with resistance are more likely to survive exposure and reproduce, increasing the frequency of resistance in the population. The change is not purposeful.
questions.difficulty: Resistance is caused only by bacteria becoming larger
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which heart chamber has the thickest muscular wall in a healthy adult, and why?
questions.option_a: Right atrium, because it receives blood from the body
questions.option_c: Left atrium, because it pumps blood to the lungs
questions.correct_answer: Right ventricle, because it pumps blood through the aorta
questions.distractor_rationales: The left ventricle generates the pressure needed to send blood around the systemic circuit, so its muscular wall is the thickest.
questions.difficulty: Left ventricle, because it pumps blood through the systemic circulation
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the main function of the atrioventricular valves during ventricular contraction?
questions.option_a: To allow blood to flow back into the atria
questions.option_c: To prevent blood from flowing backward into the atria
questions.correct_answer: To send blood directly from the aorta into the ventricles
questions.distractor_rationales: When the ventricles contract, the atrioventricular valves close to prevent backflow into the atria. The semilunar valves open to allow ejection into the great arteries.
questions.difficulty: To oxygenate blood inside the heart
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes an artery?
questions.option_a: It carries blood away from the heart
questions.option_c: It always carries oxygen-rich blood
questions.correct_answer: It has valves along its entire length
questions.distractor_rationales: Arteries are defined by carrying blood away from the heart. Pulmonary arteries carry oxygen-poor blood, so oxygen content is not the defining feature.
questions.difficulty: It carries blood toward the heart
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is one major function of the lymphatic system?
questions.option_a: Producing red blood cells in all adult tissues
questions.option_c: Returning excess tissue fluid to the bloodstream
questions.correct_answer: Pumping blood from the heart to the lungs
questions.distractor_rationales: Lymphatic vessels collect excess interstitial fluid and return it to the circulation. Lymphatic organs also contribute to immune defence.
questions.difficulty: Producing digestive enzymes in the stomach
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which cells differentiate to become the main antibody-secreting cells in a humoral immune response?
questions.option_a: Red blood cells
questions.option_c: Platelets
questions.correct_answer: Neutrophils
questions.distractor_rationales: Activated B lymphocytes can differentiate into plasma cells, which secrete antibodies that bind specific antigens.
questions.difficulty: Plasma cells derived from activated B lymphocytes
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why can a secondary immune response to a previously encountered antigen be faster than the first response?
questions.option_a: Memory lymphocytes remain after the first response and can respond rapidly
questions.option_c: The antigen becomes a red blood cell
questions.correct_answer: The body stops recognizing the antigen
questions.distractor_rationales: Memory B and T lymphocytes can persist after the initial exposure and respond more rapidly when the same antigen is encountered again.
questions.difficulty: All antibodies remain permanently at the same concentration
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which immune cell type can directly destroy body cells infected by a virus as part of specific cellular immunity?
questions.option_a: Erythrocytes
questions.option_c: Platelets
questions.correct_answer: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes
questions.distractor_rationales: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes recognize infected cells displaying relevant antigen fragments and can induce those cells to die, limiting infection spread.
questions.difficulty: Mature red blood cells
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which feature of an alveolus most directly supports rapid diffusion of oxygen into the blood?
questions.option_a: A thick wall made of several tissue layers
questions.option_c: A thin moist surface closely associated with capillaries
questions.correct_answer: A surface with no blood supply
questions.distractor_rationales: Thin moist alveolar walls and a dense capillary network create a short diffusion distance and maintain gas exchange.
questions.difficulty: A small surface area and low ventilation
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: During normal inspiration, what happens when the diaphragm contracts?
questions.option_a: The thoracic cavity becomes smaller and pressure rises
questions.option_c: The lungs actively push air out
questions.correct_answer: The diaphragm moves upward and relaxes
questions.distractor_rationales: Diaphragm contraction flattens it and increases thoracic volume. The resulting pressure decrease allows air to flow into the lungs.
questions.difficulty: Thoracic volume increases and pressure inside the lungs falls
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which change is associated with long-term exposure to tobacco smoke?
questions.option_a: Improved ciliary clearance in the airways
questions.option_c: Damage to airway cilia and reduced efficiency of normal airway cleaning
questions.correct_answer: A permanent increase in alveolar surface area
questions.distractor_rationales: Tobacco smoke can damage airway cilia and impair the mechanisms that help remove mucus and trapped particles. This is a harmful effect, not a preparation strategy or a recommendation.
questions.difficulty: Complete prevention of respiratory infection
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the main digestive role of bile?
questions.option_a: It digests proteins into amino acids
questions.option_c: It breaks starch into maltose
questions.correct_answer: It emulsifies large fat droplets into smaller droplets
questions.distractor_rationales: Bile salts emulsify fats, increasing the surface area available to lipase. Bile is not itself a digestive enzyme.
questions.difficulty: It is a protease released by the pancreas
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which substrate is acted on by pancreatic amylase?
questions.option_a: Proteins
questions.option_c: Triglycerides
questions.correct_answer: Nucleic acids
questions.distractor_rationales: Pancreatic amylase hydrolyses starch into smaller carbohydrate products, including maltose and short oligosaccharides.
questions.difficulty: Starch
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: How do intestinal villi improve absorption?
questions.option_a: They reduce the intestine's internal surface area
questions.option_c: They increase the surface area available for absorption
questions.correct_answer: They stop all movement of digested nutrients
questions.distractor_rationales: Villi and their microvilli greatly increase the surface area across which digested nutrients can be absorbed.
questions.difficulty: They convert every nutrient into glucose
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: A human gene is inserted into a suitable microorganism so the organism produces human insulin. Which biotechnology approach is being used?
questions.option_a: Selective breeding only
questions.option_c: Recombinant DNA technology
questions.correct_answer: Simple filtration
questions.distractor_rationales: Recombinant DNA methods introduce a gene into a host organism so that the host can produce a useful protein such as insulin.
questions.difficulty: Artificial pollination
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why can a monoclonal antibody be useful in a diagnostic test?
questions.option_a: It binds many unrelated targets equally
questions.option_c: It destroys every cell in a sample
questions.correct_answer: It can bind a particular target molecule with high specificity
questions.distractor_rationales: A monoclonal antibody population recognizes a particular antigenic target, allowing that target to be detected in a test.
questions.difficulty: It converts RNA directly into protein
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of including a suitable antigen in a vaccine?
questions.option_a: To train the immune system to recognize the target and develop immune memory
questions.option_c: To replace all white blood cells
questions.correct_answer: To guarantee that a person can never become infected
questions.distractor_rationales: A vaccine presents an antigen or instructions for making an antigen so the immune system can develop a targeted response and memory. Protection is not an absolute guarantee.
questions.difficulty: To act as a digestive enzyme
questions.source: Original Apex draft aligned to PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025; requires academic review.
